# Concat feature adoption

Reference: https://github.com/jub0t/concat at `78e4be101c2d3c41a7dc73c112c6b1f11b9ce170` (AGPL-3.0). Source inspected in concat-project/commands, concat-api/message, concat-effects, concat-speech, concat-vision and keyboard documentation. This adoption implements behavior through our existing commands and native rendering; no Concat code was copied. The machine-readable command/API inventory is concat-catalog.json. Inventory does not establish parity.

## First implementation: split all lanes at playhead

Added “Разрезать все дорожки” to the command toolbar/palette and configurable Mod+B shortcut. No selection required; only clips strictly crossing the playhead are cut. Canonical splits retain existing source-clock/animation/transition/link semantics, with linked participants cut once. Any locked participant refuses the entire operation. All edits commit once and Undo restores the full document. Exact-boundary repeat is disabled. Tests cover linked AV, one Undo and locked participant refusal. Qualification details are recorded after terminal results below.

Full Concat feature parity remains OPEN, alongside outstanding Filmcraft/WeftCut scope.

Validation: 74 tests across command registry, shortcut settings, composition state, transition splitting and App passed. Strengthened final split-all regression adds an independent overlay lane and no selection alongside linked AV: three lanes become six clips, two link groups, one Undo, exact document restoration, and atomic locked-participant refusal; final 17 focused tests passed. Production build passed (18.57s, existing chunk warnings). Initial typecheck found a test-only union flatMap type mismatch, corrected with explicit CompositionClip; rerun passed with zero errors/warnings. Final test-strengthening typecheck pending. Design token/lifecycle checks and git diff --check passed. No native renderer changes or whole-Concat parity claim.

Final strengthened-test typecheck exited 0: zero errors and zero warnings. All owned Concat inspection/qualification processes are terminal. Full feature adoption remains OPEN.

## Reattach synchronized source audio

New “Вернуть звук в видео” controls in both video and audio inspectors use a canonical atomic command. Detachment now creates/extends the existing link group, preserving existing group membership and one audio owner. Reattach accepts either selected member, transfers gain/pan and deep-cloned automation, deletes only the matched linked sound, prunes links through canonical deletion, selects the video, and commits once. Input stays unchanged on any failure. Unrelated same-source audio is never guessed as a detached counterpart.

Admission preserves rendering: currently embedded audio belongs to the active primary video; unsupported overlay/muted/disabled tracks, changed source spans/speed/ramp/reverse, locked members, fades, crossfades, DSP, ducking, voice/pitch/tone processing and non-dialogue role are refused with a reason. These remaining processed/multistream scenarios are open feature work, not qualified Concat parity. Detachment now preserves enabled state and uses existing keyframe clone routines (instead of structuredClone on reactive proxies); speed-ramp points are copied explicitly.

Validation: 98 tests across state, imported AV pairing, pure reattach admission and mounted inspector passed; state tests exercise mix automation and one Undo/Redo; inspector test clicks the audio-side button and restores the full document with Undo. Typecheck zero errors/warnings; production build passed13.86s(existing chunk warnings); git diff --check passed. An initial test snapshot failed on a reactive proxy and was corrected to serialized document snapshots; test gain editing now uses the canonical gain command. Stronger reverse/speed/pre-existing-automation scenario pending final rerun.

AI scope remains included in the requested Concat adoption. Local whisper-cli is available on this host; offline ASR integration, model management and captions pipeline still require implementation and verification. This observation is not an implemented ASR feature.

## Join compatible fragments and preserve split animation

Added “Соединить фрагменты” to toolbar/palette and configurableMod+J. The command stages all changes, expands linked AV participants, groups by lane, checks touching placements, contiguous original source order (forward/reverse), matching source/settings/names and rebased animation context, keeps the first ID, joins source spans, coalesces corresponding link groups, prunes obsolete names and commits oneUndo. Locked participants, gaps/overlaps, source jumps, differing settings and unrelated clips inside the span refuse atomically. This is lossless joining; render consolidation of arbitrary clips is a separate outstanding feature.

Remaining admission work is explicit: source speed ramps (also refused by originalConcatMergeClips), selected transitions, internal audio fades/crossfades, processed image/native-effect layers and responsive/rolling graphic clocks are not yet joined. No claim of completeMergeClips/ConsolidateClipsparity.

Found and reproduced a prerequisite playback bug:splitAnimatableValue discarded surrounding keys, turning a crossing animation segment into different endpoint values after a cut. Sixnewlinear/ease/bounceframe-samplingregressionsfailedbeforefix. Split now retains full context and only rebases the right clock using the existing keyframe shift contract. Existing partition-shape tests were replaced with sampled-value assertions; audio/mask/source split tests likewise verify actual interpolation, not dropped-key arrays. Existing custom-timebase shift quantization is unchanged; arbitrary fractional source-clock phase is not newly qualified.

## Original / processed-copy switching

Added explicit retain-original option when replacing a clip, plus inspector toggle between original and processed-copy sources. First original is retained across repeated copy replacements; ordinary replacement clears the pair. Switching preserves current authored placement, transforms/effects/animation, and refuses locked or incompatible/short sources through the same replacement command. This is user-supplied processed-media comparison, not an implemented learned enhancement model. Stored metadata.mediaVersions maps clip IDs to originalSourceId/copySourceId; native metadata DTO now serializes the typed map and accepts legacy omission (empty map is omitted). Updated30 existing native metadata struct literals with empty default values to preserve old fixtures. Frontend validation checks clip/source references and active source membership. Split/duplicate/copy-insert retain pairs and both sources, delete/join prune absorbed records, merge refuses mismatched saved pairs, relink rewrites active and inactive references, and inserted holds inherit the source versions. Pure tests cover repeated copy replacement, ordinary clearing, split/duplicate/join/delete/relink/cross-project paste and wire metadata; mounted controls verify toggle and two successive Undo operations. ## Remove timelines with explicit placement handling

Added Remove Timeline control and pure removeTimeline staging. Last timeline and unknown IDs refuse; active removal chooses next then previous neighbor, while deleting an unselected timeline preserves its current view/time. Removing the project root chooses a remaining unreferenced root, avoiding an invalid root that is still placed elsewhere. Referenced timelines refuse by default; UI exposes an explicit checkbox with placement count to also remove all direct placements of that timeline. Only those instance records are removed; unrelated clips/compositions remain intact. Removed timeline and transitive ancestor render bindings are invalidated selectively; unrelated bindings remain. One Undo/Redo restores document, placements, output bindings and affected active selection/time. Native validation precedes commit and failures retain all state.

## Persistent narration assets and canonical timeline insertion (2026-10-20)

Added authenticated PUT /speech/narration-assets for explicitly accepted24kHzmono WAV,64MiB/10min admission and synchronous upload resource slot. Host-generated IDs/paths only. Original files publish into sources/spaces/{space}/{uuid}.wav with0600 permissions, synchronized bytes, no-replace link and owned staging cleanup. Cleanup guards acquire ownership only after successful create/link, preserving pre-existing files on failure. Space claim precedes library visibility; flat public source path never exists. Uses existing library/file/search/export Space authorization instead of inventing a separate bypass. Project editor rights rechecked before visibility. Ordinary Space projects reuse their Space. ### 2026-10-24 — editor native DSP playback and bounded browser qualification

Connected the flat composition preview to the native PCM transport whenever an
eligible enabled audio clip has an active DSP effect. The authored wire serializer
and role-mix semantics are reused, including preview role gain overrides. Native
mixed audio suppresses raw audio elements and hard-mutes embedded video audio;
ordinary preview playback returns when no eligible active DSP remains.

`NativeAudioPreview` keeps at most two two-second blocks, one request in flight,
and schedules actual AudioBufferSourceNodes through the existing shared master
mute/limiter/meter graph. AudioContext time drives the editor playhead. Initial
buffering and underruns hold video and timeline time. Pause, seeks, edits, token
changes and teardown abort old requests and stop old nodes; stale responses cannot
start audio. Errors pause transport and remain visible rather than playing dry
media. Fractional-sample composition tails explicitly finish transport.

### 2026-10-24 — nested timeline native transport and continuous frame queue

Added nested-editor play/pause, a bounded playhead slider and authoritative native
focused-duration lookup. The shared PCM controller now forwards an explicit
compositionId. Nested transport uses the same two-block AudioContext clock,
private source checks and DSP mixer as flat playback. External seeks invalidate
old buffers and frame requests; navigation/session boundaries and edit locks pause
playback; end-of-duration completes and replay starts from zero. Close/unmount
stops requests, nodes and the animation frame. Invalid duration and audio failures
remain visible and stop transport.

Native frame preview now distinguishes continuous playback ticks from semantic
scope changes. Playback ticks coalesce into one running request plus the latest
pending request, allowing completed frames to reach the canvas without repeated
per-tick cancellation. Explicit seeks, pause, project/output/focus/session changes
and teardown still abort old scopes. This prevents request starvation; it does
not assert a display frame rate or exact audio/video presentation latency.

Targeted tests: 15/15 across nested transport, frame queue and PCM controller.
They cover focused clock selection, seeks/navigation, authored completion and
replay, stale/invalid duration responses, errors, continuous frame coalescing,
explicit seek cancellation and the explicit PCM focus parameter. Initial unit
failures exposed the Vitest SSR `untrack` stub in the test environment; the test
now uses Svelte's actual client untrack. The navigation test waits for the newly
selected timeline's duration before pressing its disabled play button.

Real loopback backend/FFmpeg/Chromium gate: 2/2 integration tests passed, 0 ignored,
5.98 seconds. In addition to the flat private-source gate, a child placed one

### 2026-10-24 — native Concat Distorted and shared lookahead limiter

Added `concat.distorted` as a static native DSP effect with original Drive 0..100,
default 50, step 1 and disabled parameter animation. The original package has no
short `distorted` alias; qualification explicitly checks canonical lookup and the
absence of that alias. Audio processing owns float volume precision, the six-bit
soft quantizer, default sample-reduction arithmetic, linked double-precision
limiting and uncompensated audible delay. Drive zero retains the original
quantization behavior rather than introducing an identity shortcut. The existing
native chain, PCM preview and WAV export paths host this processor; no runtime
FFmpeg distortion/limiter graph is introduced. Existing Filmcraft algorithms are
unchanged. Full source-age replay is used for cold Distorted seeks within the
existing six-hour/cancellation budget; canonical EOF truncates its delayed output.

The shared `concat_limiter.rs` uses fixed candidate storage, cached channel peaks
and an equal-ceiling fast path. The mono finite-ring sentinel behavior is
intentional parity, including its attenuation quirk on sustained peaks. Its
reference contract is FFmpeg n9.0.2 `af_alimiter.c` (default attack/release,
latency=false); quantizer reference is `af_acrusher.c`. Primary source:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/n9.0.2/libavfilter/af_alimiter.c
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/n9.0.2/libavfilter/af_acrusher.c
These are qualification references; the production implementation is owned Rust.

The standalone real-FFmpeg limiter matrix passed 120 rate/channel/signal/limit
combinations and 2199780 double PCM values at unchanged absolute 2e-12, plus reset.
The initial monotonic-event prototype failed mono sustained peaks; subsequent
unbounded/debug iterator prototypes were explicitly terminated while CPU-active
and retained as negative evidence (`concat-distorted-native.log`,
`concat-distorted-native-optimized.log`, sample in

thresholds; no test timeout or tolerance was increased. Its first 60-case native
Distorted run completed in 3.57 seconds, and the standalone limiter in 5.51
seconds. These are verification runtimes, not a paired production speedup claim.

### 2026-10-24 — Enhance Voice compressor prerequisite

Added an independently authored linked RMS downward compressor in Rust for
the original Enhance Voice settings. It averages channel magnitudes before
squaring the detector, preserves recursive attack/release state, and uses an
analytic logarithmic soft-knee curve joining the unity and compressed slopes.
It performs no allocation in frame processing and reset clears the envelope.

`concat_compressor::actual_enhance_voice_compressor_matches_owned_stage`
passed 32 actual FFmpeg comparisons: 8000/44100/48000/192000 Hz, mono/stereo,
threshold/ratio pairs corresponding to amount 0/40/60/100, attack 15 ms and
release 120 ms. The synthetic signal includes low-level input, knee crossing,
overrange peaks and a long silent release segment. Compared 3,520,416 double
PCM values plus reset replay at unchanged 2e-12 tolerance. The terminal result
is 1 passed / 0 failed in `backend/target/qualification-logs/concat-compressor.log`.

### 2026-10-24 — Native streaming rational resampler for pitch-family graphs

Added an independently authored Rust streaming resampler prerequisite for
Pitch, Chipmunk, Deep and Sweet. It uses the original 32-tap/default Kaiser
beta-9 model with cutoff 0.97, rate-dependent even tap counts, exact rational
phase counts capped at 1024, interpolated phase banks when required, and float
convolution/interpolation arithmetic. Kaiser I0 is computed natively; no FFT,
resampling library or FFmpeg DSP is called in production. Identity rate pairs
bypass resampling exactly.

The adapter keeps only the filter's input window after processing bounded input
chunks, emits before EOF when enough input is available, supports reset and
an independent empty EOF marker, and reflects the original left/right edges.
It also preserves the original zero-output behavior for inputs too short to
initialize the filter. Output length is derived from available reflected input,
not imposed by a rounded duration or padded silence.

fresh Cargo build: 176 actual FFmpeg cases, 11 input/output rate pairs including

### 2026-10-25 — Original planar decoder layout through Pitch

Investigating adjacent format negotiation exposed a missing input property:
packing decoded ALAC S16P into disk PCM preserved values and packets but lost
the original planar layout used to select the first resampler output. On the
qualified AArch64 SWR path, float->planar-S16 vector conversion rounds each
channel, whereas packed multichannel conversion selects upper halfwords.
Scalar tails also have distinct handling. Treating those formats identically
would introduce common one-LSB differences before tempo.

independently of the physical packed spool. Source-preserving and negotiated
float readers configure only the first Pitch resampler with this layout; the
second resampler retains its explicitly selected packed output. Seek/reset
preserves that configuration. Existing constructors default to the packed
raw-PCM profile, preserving earlier gates.

from source in, retaining its original frame boundaries.

### 2026-10-25: overlong embedded-video fades and source clock distinction

Pinned source has different overlong fade-out clocks: `concat-host/src/playback.rs` uses `(duration-local)/fade_out`, while `concat-media/src/audio.rs` exports `afade` starting at `max(duration-fade_out,0)`. Packet processors now expose their retained clip metadata and deliver processed, gain/pan-applied transition-side blocks to the shared transition mixer. The mixer combines packet and fixed-frame sides within their original group and applies independent window replacement once. Packet sides are no longer summed unconditionally after transition processing. Source-typed decode/DSP paths and per-clip packet state remain intact; transition metadata changes only host mixing. Additional side blocks are checked for group metadata, finite values, exact frame count and aggregate layer/block budget. The former packet transition admission refusal is removed; packet tempo/reverse still explicitly refuses.

`packet-transition-streams.log` passes both existing packet/Echo private-preview regressions and both expanded multistream integrations. The transition matrix covers Echo/Echo, neutral Pitch/Pitch, +2-semitone Pitch/Echo, and default Loudness/Loudness on distinct selected mono float32 streams of the same registered MOV. Each mode covers enabled and disabled outgoing sides and both halves of the independent dissolve. Actual private PCM and public WAV match independently processed sides followed by Constant Power mixing; an unrelated dry audio track is preserved in each mode. `packet-transition-nonzero-reference.log` reruns the multistream suite with an explicit nonzero-reference requirement for every mode/block, preventing a vacuous silence comparison. Existing 2e-7 PCM and PCM16 quantization tolerances remain unchanged.

These gates qualify finite unit-speed, clip-bounded sequential transitions and processing placement; they do not independently requalify the DSP algorithms. Packet tempo/reverse, all transition kernels, overlapping/nested/offset and mixed-format processed sides, arbitrary DSP chains/automation, video-container delivery of this exact matrix and full application parity remain open. All generated media and captures remain temporary or ignored; no large fixture is tracked.

### Rational VFR source-picture pacer (2026-10-26)

Added `domain::concat_video_pacer`, following original `concat-media::next_paced`:
select the last presentation picture at/before the 10 Hz target, show the first
picture before its initial PTS, normalize stream-start ticks, and stop at the last
PTS plus one analysis interval. Integer/rational comparisons avoid rounding a future
picture (including a 1 ns difference) onto the grid. Only current and lookahead
pictures are retained; input decoding errors propagate. The analysis-frame budget
is not incorrectly applied to the number of decoded source frames.

Tests cover VFR holds/EOF, stream offset, sub-microsecond boundaries, missing PTS,
decode errors, long decoded input with a one-frame analysis request, and a real
FFV1 VFR red/green/blue fixture decoded via FFmpeg/FFprobe. That fixture must select
red/green/green/blue at 0/100/200/300 ms. The pacer is a generic Rust decoder adapter;
production video decode/analysis/HTTP wiring is still pending. No new native codec
or full video parity is claimed.

### Host decoding adapter for source-PTS analysis runs (2026-10-26)

Added `services::concat_video_sample`: fingerprints source/codec tools, probes integer
presentation timestamps into a monitored bounded staging file, selects source
ordinals through the Rust pacer, decodes unique pictures with an external filter
file, and writes duplicates on the exact 10 Hz grid into private RGBA staging.
Sampled output records encoded-video and decoded-RGBA hashes, dimensions/start/count;
owned staging is removed on drop/error. Reads and selected-frame staging are bounded.
Current decoder integration uses host FFmpeg/FFprobe, not a new Rust video codec.

Source review found that original nonzero `starting_at` first discards pictures
before the series start, then applies the pacer's first-future-picture fallback.
The adapter mirrors this explicitly. A series beyond EOF returns no sampled run.
Tests cover VFR colors, stream PTS offset, nonzero series seek semantics, bad source
identity, tiny staging budget/cleanup, and actual sampled-RGBA -> RVM -> verified
mask run. Production HTTP video analysis/cache/export wiring remains open; source
PTS probing currently scans the source and seek-performance parity is unqualified.

### Automatic video range fill — 2026-10-26

`RunCache::fill_missing` connects the global missing-grid planner to source-PTS sampling, fresh native RVM recurrence per contiguous missing run, verification and cache insertion. Existing instants are reused; EOF produces an explicit empty-run count. Completed runs remain available if a later run fails or is cancelled, matching the source host's incremental mask store. Source fingerprint and runtime identity are checked even when nothing is missing; all work shares a caller deadline. Source ACL/Analysis admission remain caller responsibilities. This currently supports the Person/RVM family only, without persistent cache, HTTP/editor orchestration or Auto/Object/Selfie video selection.

Qualification: real encoded VFR + pinned native RVM test passed in 5.98s (`concat-video-fill-live.log`, ignored local logs directory). A cache containing 100/200/300 ms automatically fills only 0 ms, reports 400 ms as EOF, resolves nearest masks across the successful separate runs, and a repeat 0–300 ms request reports zero analysed runs/frames. Wrong video/runtime identities are rejected even for empty requested ranges. Regression suites `concat_video_masks` and `concat_video_pacer`: 6 passed, 2 opt-in cases ignored; the real sampler/RVM case above ran separately. Full parity remains unproven.

### Persistent video-mask generations — 2026-10-26

`RunCache::publish` writes a fresh private UUID generation, copies each independently verified mask plane into create-new files, syncs files, verifies complete mask identities, and writes the strict versioned manifest last. A server-owned `PublishedCache` receipt binds the manifest hash, encoded-video hash and runtime hash. `RunCache::restore` accepts that trusted receipt (not client paths), bounds manifest/total bytes, verifies receipt identity and every native mask run, then reconstructs the disjoint timeline. Failed publication cleans only its owned new directory. Restored handles and receipt drops leave published files intact. Callers still need project ACL, trusted receipt persistence, generation retention/garbage collection, and restart discovery. Directory fsync/crash durability is not established by these tests.

Actual encoded VFR/pinned RVM qualification passed (1 test, 5.48s; ignored local `concat-video-cache-persistence-live.log`). Test destroys the entire original owned analysis cache before restoring published masks, checks grid coverage and lookup, rejects cancelled/under-budget publication, rejects under-budget restore, changed manifest and changed mask bytes, and rejects mutation through an already-restored provider. Failed restore does not remove published files. This proves service persistence/reopen, not a running application restart or project HTTP/UI integration. No tracked media/model fixtures were added.

### Project video-cache registry — 2026-10-26

Added additive SQLite `concat_video_project_caches` registry and internal `handlers/concat_video_cache.rs` bridge. Publication resolves source IDs through project/editor/source access, fingerprints the current source, publishes a new verified generation, rechecks source/revision/access and registers using an INSERT SELECT constrained by current editor membership, project revision and project source reference. Failed registration removes only the new generation. Restoration discovers the newest matching encoded-video/runtime generation using server metadata, validates the UUID basename, restores against the trusted manifest identity and rechecks access/source. Changed video/runtime yields a cache miss; corrupt matching data remains an error. Registered generations are retained, not overwritten. Runtime hash is an internal host argument, not a public request field.

Actual VFR/RVM integration passed (1 test, 13.06s; ignored `concat-video-project-cache-live.log`): private project/library source registration, empty discovery, publication, original temporary cache destruction, a newly opened SQLite connection restoring saved coverage/masks, outsider publish/read refusal, unrelated source refusal, stale revision refusal, runtime mismatch miss and replaced encoded-source miss. Existing service corruption/budget/cleanup assertions also passed. This is a DB reopen in the same test process, not a complete AppState/process restart or public HTTP/editor flow. Generation garbage collection, source-space revocation transaction races, full restart discovery, video cutout command/UI/preview/export and other model families remain open.

### Native immutable completed-frame checkpoints — 2026-10-26

### Bounded descriptor ownership for per-frame mask caches — 2026-10-26

VerifiedMaskRun now retains its bounded path/layout and verified per-plane hashes rather than an open File for every run. Initial opening still reads and validates every mask plane. A later lookup opens only its selected file, refuses a non-regular or wrong-size file, verifies the requested plane hash, checks size again and closes the descriptor before returning mask bytes. Unix opens use O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, preventing final-component symlink following and blocking special-file opens if a path is replaced around admission. File removal/replacement now fails closed instead of silently continuing through an old retained inode. Cache identity serialization and immutable generation format are unchanged.

A separate child test lowers its own RLIMIT_NOFILE to at most64, retains512 verified runs and reads every one successfully; the parent process limits remain untouched. Dedicated gates reject renamed/replaced content, missing paths, same-content symlinks, size drift and directory replacement while permitting an exact valid file to be reopened. Initial unit integration passed5 tests with the actual-model case explicitly ignored (`concat-lazy-mask-descriptors.log`). Final qualification included all gates plus actual native RVM/provider behavior, live cancellation/prefix publication/255-instant retry and the existing VFR/router/preview/FFV1+PCM/export/recovery path (`concat-lazy-mask-live-regression.log`); all passed. The live prefix test took25.54s and mask/provider target6 tests1.20s. Logs remain ignored artifacts.

This removes linear descriptor retention, not file count or total storage costs. ### Incremental immutable project generations — 2026-10-26

Project cache publication now prepares schema2 generations containing only newly appended runs plus a canonical generation-name/manifest-hash reference to the accepted prefix. The initial/full standalone schema1 format and filenames remain supported; a different storage root or explicit unchanged re-publication produces a fresh full generation. A sealed prepared-publication cursor belongs to one RunCache instance and is accepted only after SQLite registration succeeds. Failed registration removes only its newly prepared directory and leaves the previous cursor and all old data intact. Files are synced before manifest publication; Unix generation/root directories are also synced before registration.

Restore walks parent generations iteratively, enforcing manifest hashes, exact source/model/runtime identity, cumulative run counts, total reachable byte/frame bounds, canonical UUID basenames, no cycles and real directories. It validates every mask plane before exposing the reconstructed cache. Insertion order/content identity is preserved across restore; descriptors remain lazy. Parent manifests and masks are immutable and must be retained while descendants refer to them. No generation GC is introduced.

### 2026-10-28 — recover ordinary smart strokes before the start acknowledgement

The panel now writes a validated version-3 intent before submitting SAM: stable
operation UUID, exact saved revision, original source identity, cursor, complete
points/tool/size and the captured document receipt. Once the server acknowledges,
the same localStorage entry is atomically promoted to the existing accepted v2
shape with the same ID and operationId. Legacy v1/v2 records remain readable.
Resuming an unacknowledged intent verifies the unchanged local document and
reissues the identical operation; it never fabricates a job ID or seed clock.
A newer accepted phase written by another observer is used under the existing
Web Lock. Unknown/damaged records and newer IDs remain preserved.

This connects the durable server operation API added in the preceding work:
optional operationId on smart-region POST; authenticated project/actor-scoped
lookup and cancellation routes; SQLite receipt/reservation bound to the complete
request digest and source hash. A reservation fixes one server-owned job ID,
including recovery between reservation and enqueue. Changed parameters under the
same operation conflict. Existing jobs are returned without selecting a new model
or depending on the short job-dedupe TTL. Replays dispatch only the existing
pending outbox item. Cancellation records a tombstone even before the POST arrives;
post-enqueue and worker-start checks also honor it. Future attachment checks reject
cancelled operations. This is one durable task identity, not a claim that inference
cannot restart after a worker/process crash.

Explicit panel cancellation uses that operation ID even when jobId is unknown.
Successful cancellation removes the matching local record and its stale lost-ACK
error; a newer editor error is preserved. Failed cancellation retains the intent.
Scope changes/unmount still stop observation without cancelling durable work.
Storage quota/refusal retains foreground processing with a warning, so recovery is
not promised when the browser could not persist the record. General revision
rebasing, token-rotation discovery and atomic cancel-vs-already-committing-edit
semantics are not added. Cancellation does not undo an already saved stroke.

## 2026-10-28 — native caption pixels and lossless video export qualification

Closed the earlier native-render-pixel evidence gap for the caption workflow exercised in `frontend/e2e/real-caption-lanes.spec.ts`. This milestone adds regression evidence; it does not add another application feature or establish complete source-app typography parity.

The actual authorized Rust `/api/compositions/nested-preview` RGBA endpoint rendered the native project produced by the real subtitle file UI. Byte comparisons against hidden-lane controls prove the imported fractional cue is absent at 1,124,999 us, present at 1,125,000 us and absent again at its exclusive 1,875,000 us end. Each of the two overlapping existing caption lanes independently contributes visible pixels at 1.5 s. At 1,999,999 us the full frame matches the Inner-only control; at exactly 2,000,000 us it matches the Adjacent-only control. Project-wide font restyling changes actual native pixels. At 4 s the full frame matches the no-caption control because all cues ended. These are renderer/composition invariants, not golden glyph comparisons to WeftCut.

Actual `/api/compositions/nested-export` video_only jobs produced FFV1 movies for three one-frame ranges starting at 1.125, 1.875 and 2 s. FFmpeg is used only as the verification decoder in this test. Each decoded RGBA frame exactly equals the native preview at the requested microsecond timestamp. A separate bounded 320×180, 10 fps, five-second export contains exactly 50 decoded frames; twelve sampled frame ordinals (0, 10, 11, 12, 18, 19, 20, 29, 30, 39, 40, 49) are byte-identical to native previews at their corresponding 100 ms clock positions, including before/after the fractional cue, the adjacent-cue boundary and the final no-caption region.

## 2026-10-28 — owned agent work sessions and independent lightweight view

Source contract: WeftCut `d1db8020164c51ee49df9cf0143a5cbf250951a4`, `docs/adr/0065-agent-view-work-session-and-activity-are-independent.md` and `mcp-commands.ts` begin_agent_session/end_agent_session. This milestone adopts work-session ownership/lifecycle and independent layout; the ADR's separate structured activity/provenance/delta-reconciliation system remains open, rather than being claimed through the existing diagnostic log.

Added actual MCP begin_agent_session/end_agent_session tools. They require an initialized transport session so ownership is its server-assigned connection identity, not the anonymous fallback actor. The first begin creates one Pre-agent checkpoint of the actual ordinary/native document, assigns a work UUID and enters agent view. A repeat by the same owner returns the same session/checkpoint without changing the user's selected view; another owner refuses. Checkpoint-limit/invalid-reason failures do not create a work session or change layout. Work state is outside authored documents/history/checkpoints and is cleared on document-context replacement. No work idle timer was added.

Ending work is unrecorded, retains view/checkpoints/diagnostic records and does not disconnect MCP or cancel computation. Only the owner can end it unless force:true is explicit; it releases only the ending work owner's undo lock, leaving a different owner's lock intact. There are independent local end/unlock controls. Manual Editor/Agent view switching changes layout only, never creates a checkpoint/session or releases a lock. The lightweight workspace keeps project controls, native/ordinary preview, playback controls, alerts and one shared AgentPanel; other editing panes remain mounted but hidden, so switching views does not destroy running observers. The current session reason is visible independently of history locking.

Found and fixed two transport dependencies needed by this lifecycle. AgentPanel no longer serially awaits every command before polling the next: at most 32 command executions may be active (matching the bridge pending bound), while document writes still use their existing revision/hash/busy admission. Thus another initialized client can end/inspect a session while a native computation awaits validation. Definite MCP DELETE release events also travel on the existing editor heartbeat (`x-agent-released`) so a paused/full poll path cannot hold the work badge/owned lock. A late result for an already-closed request (HTTP 410 from the bridge) is discarded without replaying the operation or disconnecting the editor; it is reported as unknown-to-that-client completion, not falsely called cancelled.

Validation: final focused suites passed 72 tests (`backend/target/qualification-logs/agent-work-tests-final2.log`), including independent manual view, one checkpoint/idempotent owner, foreign refusal/force, owned versus unrelated lock release, checkpoint-limit rollback, native checkpoint targeting/context reset, definite actor release and ending work while an already-running native operation completes normally. ## 2026-10-28 — revisioned activity snapshots, deltas and renderer repair

Source contract: pinned WeftCut `d1db8020164c51ee49df9cf0143a5cbf250951a4`, main/agent/activity snapshot/publish and renderer/agent/activityStore wireAgentActivity. Added an owned local publisher/transport and a separate renderer replica. Production AgentActivityPanel now consumes detached snapshots/deltas through this boundary rather than reading owner activity/session arrays. This is the existing browser-owned editor's local event boundary; it does not claim a new remote/backend activity API.

Publisher revisions increase monotonically across project openings even though the underlying local owner resets its internal counter. Snapshots include work/session metadata, active lock reason, checkpoint summaries, activity rows with evaluated history effects, completion ordering and eviction counts. Updates include from-revision, reset, changed rows, removed IDs and authoritative row order. The renderer rejects stale events/snapshots, checks workspace and exact predecessor revision, and refuses incomplete/duplicate ordering. An accepted reset discards old context. Snapshots and event payloads are detached from owner state, including getter-backed history effects.

Wiring subscribes before the first snapshot, serializes/coalesces repairs, requests a fresh snapshot on a revision gap, and reconciles every three seconds to repair a silently dropped last event. Late old snapshots cannot replace newer events or a newer project opening. Temporary snapshot failure keeps the last valid state and retries on reconciliation. Disposal clears timers/subscriptions and ignores outstanding replies. A tracked publisher watches actual owned history membership, so Undo/Redo effect changes publish even without a new activity record. Manual editor/agent layout changes retain panel-local filter/expansion state; a project-opening reset clears the filter and completed-display limit.

Typecheck has zero errors/warnings (`agent-sync-types-final.log`), focused lint passes (`agent-sync-lint-final2.log`), listener/timer lifecycle audit passes (`agent-sync-lifecycle.log`), and diff whitespace checks pass.

Source contract: pinned WeftCut `d1db8020164c51ee49df9cf0143a5cbf250951a4`, renderer/history/historyLinkage revealAffected and state/navigation revealLayerWithoutSeek/revealTrackWithoutSelection. Added live-reference navigation from activity: resolve the first existing Layer before falling back to an existing Track, regardless of reference order. ## 2026-10-28 — scoped native MCP atomic batch engine and rehearsal

Continues the full native/general MCP scope rather than falling through to the hidden ordinary document. Open native projects now accept apply_batch/dry_run with expectedProjectHash and optional composition_id, defaulting to the root independently of the active editor view. get_project advertises nativeBatch.operations, supported constant layer patch fields, input shape and explicit limitations. The MCP catalog accepts exactly one admission token (ordinary revision or native project hash), describes native capability lookup, and grants batch/rehearsal the existing long-compute deadline. Ordinary batches reject native hash/scope fields. Native-only update_track is explicitly described; this does not claim all advertised ordinary operations are implemented natively.

The initial native engine supports 18 operation names: add/update/delete/reorder track; add/delete/move layer and grouped move; trim/split/duplicate layer; enable layers; supported scalar/text layer patch; canvas patch; add/remove transition; create/remove link. It composes existing owned native helpers. Moves use the real stateless Rust move endpoint; retained native objects are not round-tripped through simplified authoring state. New tracks/layers use existing CompositionTrack/CompositionClip authoring inputs at their insertion boundary. Operation arguments are detached before awaits. Split/duplicate auxiliary IDs are deterministic, so rehearsal and actual application agree. Unrelated composition nodes stay retained. Structural track changes rebind native ordinal matte/control references by identity and respect locked dependents instead of silently targeting another lane. Fractional canvas rates are seeded from exact rational rates, not rounded fpsMilli.

A candidate is private until admitted. dry_run performs native Rust duration/document validation and rechecks context without history/cache mutation. apply_batch validates natively and commits the entire candidate once through the existing guarded native apply path, with one Undo/cache invalidation and one activity history ID. A failed operation or native validation leaves document/history/rendered-output caches unchanged. A stale hash, wrong composition scope, active foreign history lock, or editor expiration/disconnection refuses; the existing native generation/reference checks still prevent late wrong-project commits. No-op candidate content stays out of Undo. Explicit scalar patch fields become constants only for those requested envelopes; unrelated effects/animation remain retained.

## 2026-10-28 — native scalar keyframe reads and atomic animation edits

Continues the owned native/general MCP goal using the existing scalar track, easing and tangent algorithms already adapted from pinned WeftCut. Native get_keyframes now reads scoped visual, audio and existing path-progress envelopes, returning projectHash, constant or keyframed value, authoritative signed tick/timeBase, derived local/timeline times, effective tangents, interpolation/extrapolation and canonical outgoing preset IDs. Root is the default scope, independent of the currently viewed composition; explicit scope resolves repeated layer IDs. Read-only access does not require an unlocked history. Ordinary reads refuse a native-only composition scope instead of silently ignoring it.

The native atomic batch engine adds seven operation names: upsert_keyframe, delete_keyframe, move_keyframe, edit_keyframe, set_keyframe_preset, set_keyframe_tangent_mode and edit_keyframe_tangents. They reuse shared upsert/delete, preset baking, Auto/Free solving, normalization and explicit control-point editing. Tracks retain their own timeBase and off-clip signed keys; key moves reject occupied destinations rather than merging away another key. Deleting the last key follows the existing constant-collapse behavior. Video embedded audio maps to audioGain/audioPan, audio clips to gain/pan, and existing path motion maps to transform.position.progress. Active XY position channels are addressed inside transform.position rather than shadow legacy fields; visual XY edits on an active path refuse and direct the caller to progress. The same active-channel correction applies to native static X/Y patches. Unrelated channels, path nodes, clips and composition nodes remain retained.

get_project advertises nativeBatch.keyframeEnvelopes and the expanded operation list. The MCP catalog exposes native composition scope and signed authored ticks, including optional newTick on compound edits; ordinary runtime restrictions remain enforced by their existing commands. Native writes keep the existing history-lock, expected hash, private-candidate, native Rust validation, admission recheck and one-Undo contract. Native mask envelopes remain explicitly unsupported here because retained mask effects do not expose stable authoring mask IDs; no positional ID guessing or ordinary-background fallback is introduced.

Validation: nine-file focused suite passed 102 tests (`native-keys-tests-final2.log`). New cases cover signed non-microsecond tracks and global offsets, retained extrapolation/timeBase, add/move/edit/delete and collision rollback, compound signed edits, presets and Auto/Free/explicit tangents, last-key collapse, active XY versus path progress, video/audio envelope mapping, unsupported/locked/non-finite/tangent refusal, real scoped dispatcher rehearsal/apply and Undo/Redo with repeated IDs. Tangent numerical comparison allows only expected floating normalization error (12 decimal places), rather than replacing the shared solver. Three Rust integration targets passed 1/1 each after the final catalog correction (`native-keys-catalog-final.log`), including explicit absence of nonnegative-only constraints on both move_keyframe and edit_keyframe newTick and native read scope. Existing unrelated Rust warnings remain. Final typecheck has zero errors/warnings (`native-keys-types-final2.log`), focused lint passes (`native-keys-lint-final3.log`), lifecycle audit passes (`native-keys-lifecycle.log`) and diff whitespace checks pass.

Real Chromium/Rust full gate passed 2/2 (`native-keys-browser.log`, 35.7 s and 53.0 s). The actual main app rehearses/applies opacity keys to a real native title via MCP, reads their exact clocks, verifies one Undo, and compares 320x180 native RGBA frames at the first key and midpoint against constant-opacity 0/0.5 controls byte for byte. Native trim rebases keys to -250000/+250000 ticks while retaining global 1000000/1500000 us and produces an identical later frame. An actual signed key edit is admitted, and the complete Undo chain restores every prior document. After the compound-edit catalog correction, the main-only replay passed (`native-keys-browser-final.log`, 48.2 s). A final strengthened replay also passed (`native-keys-browser-positive.log`, 48.9 s): the midpoint additionally differs from the zero-opacity control, proving the compared layer contributes visible pixels rather than accepting a vacuous invisible-layer equality. Existing batch/session/client/activity/checkpoint/viewport/navigation and caption FFV1/pixel scenarios remain passing. All owned verification handles are terminal; no large fixtures or media were added.

Remaining scope includes native RGBA/color-track operations, stable mask-effect identity and mask keyframes, full path creation/node editing through MCP, extrapolation configuration, richer source/effect/audio patches, ripple/paste/arbitrary placement recipes, full history UI and the other WeftCut/Filmcraft/Concat application gaps. Audio and path bindings have focused mapping/model validation here; this milestone does not independently establish full codec/DSP output or every path rendering mode. Scalar keyframe access/editing is concrete progress, not completion of all native tools or all three applications.

Scoped whitespace checks pass. Log: ignored backend/target/concat-source-layer-order-final-rust.log. No fixture or media added.

Authoritative remaining layer scope: ClipKind::Layer is an adjustment treatment over the composited stack strictly below its source track, not a nested timeline reference. export/flatten.rs retains only visibility, videoEffects, opacity and audio-named fadeIn/fadeOut as treatment ramps. resolve.rs computes strength as opacity times the minimum of head/tail linear ramps, with half-open visibility; keyed effect parameters use normalized clip progress. render/gpu.rs processes lower layers first, runs the chain on that accumulated backdrop and blends the treated result over the untreated backdrop. Same-track visual layers are painted after that treatment. A correct port needs explicit backdrop ownership/order and a distinction between global shader time and normalized effect-key progress. No adjustment-layer import/runtime is claimed yet. Full three-application parity remains open.

lookup/dependency loading is not qualified.

### Freeze publication: rollback reference race

Rollback now atomically checks committed composition references and installs a durable retired-source tombstone under SQLite's writer lock before deleting its generated JPEG. Composition source claims reject retired IDs, including delayed updates after the private claim has been released and legacy unowned project creation. A committed reference wins over retirement and retains the still. This closes the reference-check/delete race; it is not crash recovery for pending files or the JSON library.

### Freeze publication: startup journal reconciliation

A pending-publication journal is reserved atomically with the private source claim. Normal publication/rollback clears it only after retaining a committed resource or completing local cleanup. At server startup, before workers and request handling, reconciliation checks committed source references under the retirement transaction. Referenced JPEGs and their library entries are preserved; unused pending entries, scoped JPEGs, staging files and claims are removed. Failures retain the journal for another startup attempt. Recovery validates canonical UUIDs and the exact library storage identity before deleting resources. Missing committed resources fail startup with a repair error instead of silently deleting a project reference.

This is startup-only reconciliation, not an online sweeper or expiring lease. A second live backend process sharing storage, power-loss durability of the JSON library/directories, remote backup deletion retries and committed-file reconstruction remain unqualified. This does not implement the full source freeze head/still/tail edit or remove retained-clock admission guards.

Validation: Rust 1.89 integration gate passed 12 tests (`concat_freeze_publish`: 11, `tts_assets`: 1). New coverage aborts a real publication after library registration, reloads both stores, verifies cleanup or committed-reference retention, forces a library persistence failure and retries recovery, and checks reservation/staging/final-file phases before registration. Recovery is idempotent in these cases. Log: ignored `backend/target/concat-freeze-journal-retry-gate.log`. No tracked media/JSON fixture added. The first compile failure was confined to the test's `unwrap_err` Debug bound and corrected with a cancellation pattern match.

### Native source-document FreezeFrame clip splice

Added `concat_freeze_splice::freeze`, a Rust source-document clip operation using the qualified raw-clock/key planner and lane ripple. ### Native freeze splice and revision-bound publication

Added a typed native bridge for qualified video clips and a `concat_freeze_publish::publish_native` service entrypoint. The bridge applies source FreezeFrame semantics through existing lossless interchange checks to the selected lane; unrelated native tracks, metadata, canvas, sources and nested nodes remain outside conversion. The publisher uses its existing private JPEG reservation, source/JPEG fingerprints, cancellation, pending journal and revision CAS. Nested explicit duration is extended when the edited content outgrows it.

`metadata.concatLaneGroups` records the video/image typed siblings of one original lane. A repeated freeze rejoins only these explicit siblings for source scheduling, then updates the same typed lanes; it does not infer membership from IDs or names. Reordered, differently visible or locked siblings fail the operation. Existing metadata literals initialize this optional field empty; old serialized documents retain their previous shape.

Important limits: ordinary native controls that fail the existing lossless export check still refuse publication and must roll back the generated JPEG; this includes the current ordinary default-scale fixture. The retained-clock admission guard is unchanged. UI/API/agent wiring, group-aware general timeline edits/import/export, image-target publication, original cache-path media reuse and full export/render qualification remain open. This is not full application parity.

Actual JPEG extraction followed by native head/still/tail publication and DB reload passed for flat and nested imported Concat clips; explicit nested duration grew once and unrelated nodes were unchanged. Repeated freeze preserved the sibling image lane identity and moved the previous still. Head-derived names are copied to new parts for metadata effects. Reordered siblings and the unqualified ordinary default-scale fixture refuse rather than lose data; publication refusal removes its new JPEG/claim/journal. The first repeated-freeze test exposed omitted image playback defaults in source interchange; restoring normalized source `sourceStart=0` and `speed=1` fixed it without weakening admission. ### Revision-bound freeze HTTP command

Added authenticated `POST /api/composition-projects/:id/freeze-frame` with an 8 KiB strict JSON body: revision, optional nested compositionId, clipId and document-second time. Source/executable paths and JPEG bytes are never accepted. Owner/editor access is checked before resolving codecs or capturing; request admission shares bounded upload slots, capture/publication retain their process deadlines and shutdown cancellation, and persistence uses the qualified native publisher. Stale revisions return 409, unauthorized/read-only access 401/403, occupied admission 429 and source no-op 200 with `changed:false`. Successful responses include the committed project and private media. Added the route policy and typed frontend client helper; no UI control is connected yet.

Composition selection must match flat/nested project shape. Native conversion/admission restrictions and all previously listed group-aware editing/import/export, render/platform and full-parity gaps remain open. The HTTP endpoint does not turn the feature into general support for arbitrary native controls or retained source clocks.

### Nested editor freeze button and undoable server-response adoption

Added “Стоп-кадр по курсору” to the native nested clip panel for one unlocked video selection in a saved authenticated project. The action preflights the complete saved revision/document/name against the local snapshot, invokes the revision-bound freeze API, verifies the returned project/revision/new image/time and unchanged unrelated compositions, then adopts it as one Undo/Redo record. Existing outputs are invalidated; the new still is selected and the library refreshed. Local Undo retains the latest server revision so a subsequent save uses the correct CAS base. Agent history locks are checked before sending the mutation.

Pending replies do not overwrite edited documents, renamed/replaced projects or closed sessions. If a committed response arrives after local edits, those edits remain and the editor reports that the server saved the still and must be refreshed before another write. Unsaved documents are rejected before mutation; no-op responses add no history. Frontend request/reply tests do not prove browser playback or full render/export parity.

### Rational native keyframe clock groundwork

Added an immutable rational affine clock mapping `authored_us=(local_us*num+offset)/den`, with exact composition of tail offsets and hold retiming. Prepared samplers validate the track/numeric domain once. Native sampling rounds only after applying the rational mapping; exact Concat/Filmcraft source modes retain fractional source TPS and their separate evaluator policy. Identity native sampling preserves the legacy `sample_seconds` path. No persisted track field or browser wire format is activated by this change, and off-grid freeze remains refused until clock ownership, serialization, browser editing and rendering are integrated.

The existing exact keyframe source sampler now shares an authored-coordinate numerator/denominator evaluator; its old callers pass the same fixed denominator and preserve operation order. Clock rate/offset/track/key bounds prove products fit i128; out-of-domain samples refuse instead of truncating/wrapping. Tests include negative half ticks, composition/reduction, loop/ping-pong extrapolation and extreme numeric inputs.

Validation: 37 Rust 1.89 integration tests passed with original retime records enabled (`native_keyframe_clock`: 6, `native_video_freeze`: 9, `concat_temporal_source_clock`: 4, `concat_source_visual_clock`: 2, `concat_freeze_publish`: 16). Negative controls demonstrate that rounding a 100 ms/24 Hz cut to integer keys selects the wrong value and flooring a fractional hold time base also changes values; another control detects premature rounding to source TPS. Existing Filmcraft original-parameter fixture bits and source visual/temporal controls remained exact. Initial test expected an incompletely reduced fraction; corrected the expected canonical form. Log: ignored `backend/target/native-keyframe-clock-qualified-gate.log`. No new media/large fixture added. This is prerequisite clock machinery, not completed off-grid editing or full three-application parity.

### Native fractional FreezeFrame producer, pan lattice and scalar inspector

Native keyed-video FreezeFrame now emits `sampleClock` when a cut or replay duration is off the authored key grid, and composes an existing clock for repeated freezes. Exact-grid pose/gain edits retain the earlier representation. The inserted image replays the complete original pose/opacity curve over its one-second hold, while the video tail retains its original animation phase. Existing native profile restrictions on effects, paths, playback, source/raster budgets and source-clock ownership remain in place.

Pan needs an additional invariant: its ten-millisecond coefficient lattice belongs to the original authored clock. Native freeze therefore retains a clock for keyed tail pan even on exact key-grid cuts. Native PCM applies the clock before selecting the authored coefficient cell and samples the unclocked author-grid nodes, preserving the interpolation phase. Flat export now selects the native audio path for clocked gain/pan on eligible audible tracks; this does not make previously inaudible secondary video owners independent.

Added a native scalar inspector for position, scale, rotation, opacity, gain and pan. It displays mapped local seconds, inserts the actual sampled curve value at the cursor, moves/deletes keys, chooses easing presets and edits extrapolation. It uses the original curve for sampling, rather than reconstructed inspection rows. Edits validate through the backend, invalidate rendered outputs, create one Undo entry and retain Redo. Locked tracks, channel/context changes during validation and a newly acquired agent history lock prevent commits. This inspector does not claim custom tangent-handle UI or path-progress authoring parity.

### MCP native FreezeFrame and pending-publication context ownership

Advertised `freeze_frame` as a separate MCP tool for an authenticated, saved native project, with required `expectedProjectHash`, `clipId` and integer `time_us`; optional `composition_id` defaults to the project root. Pending server replies now recheck cursor, active composition, history ownership and caller admission before changing local state. If the server has committed after a context change, expiry or newly acquired foreign history lock, local state stays intact and the caller is told to reload before another write. An internal publication observer also lets an agent report a committed mutation after the editor has closed, without populating the closed/new editor's history or error state. Requests expiring during saved-document preflight never send the publication POST.

### Live native compositor preview for scalar tangent gestures

Scalar graph gestures now publish a temporary native project through the existing owner/gesture-scoped effect preview queue. The preview project is constructed by the same native tangent operation used for commit, retains the base document and sample clock, and is bound to composition, playhead time and authenticated session. The active canvas receives the draft with rendered-output cache bypassed; the reference canvas keeps the committed document. Repeated pointer movements coalesce while an in-flight render can still deliver an intermediate frame of the same gesture. Cancelled-gesture frames cannot replace the restored base frame.

The temporary project stays outside the authoring document, saved project, agent hash and Undo stacks. On release it remains visible until validation resolves; success commits one history edit and refusal restores the base preview. Clearing a gesture is scoped by owner and identity. Channel/project/playhead/session changes, track/history locks and unmount clear it. Scalar edits also recheck the authenticated session at commit, so changing account while validation is pending cannot apply the earlier local edit.

### Position conversion retains native scalar clocks and authored-grid rounding

Conversion requests now carry `sampleGrid` for each animated scalar channel: authored time base, rational rate and signed phase. Integer half-tick arithmetic uses signed i128, matching native renderer ties including negative offsets. Key, repeat and rest boundaries are mapped back into local time before fitting. Unclocked animated channels also send an identity clock with their original grid; fitting no longer silently treats a coarse authored grid as continuous microseconds. Existing callers without `sampleGrid` retain their prior continuous conversion input semantics.

The frontend transports authored coordinates and clock metadata; fitting and residual measurement remain in Rust. Converted tracks are emitted on the local microsecond grid without inheriting the source clock a second time. Packing/unpacking retains optional grid metadata. Native agent conversion forwards an optional cancellation signal and rejects an aborted result before constructing a candidate.

### Native scalar graph edge autoscroll

Graph point drags, direct Bezier-handle drags and two-dimensional selection boxes now edge-pan the same bounded time viewport as the lanes. The parent accepts panning only against the expected current view with no competing parent gesture; only the owning graph context updates its pinned range. Pointer time movement includes accumulated viewport offset, while the value axis remains frozen. Bezier controls convert this accumulated time through the original channel/segment clock. Selected source-point elements and the owning tangent handle remain mounted for capture while their original positions leave the viewport. Box hit-testing includes initially hidden authored keys, retains its temporal anchor and fixed value bounds, and publishes only selection on release. All animation callbacks validate source/session/selection/viewport ownership and frozen SVG geometry; cancel, capture loss, resize, explicit navigation, close or unmount terminate animation. Point/tangent edits still use one validated native transaction; box navigation alone does not edit/render/cache-invalidate the document.

### Creating source curves directly from empty graphs

All 16 source editors now retain an insertion-capable graph when their source run is empty or its last key was deleted. Empty graphs use the parameter's authored domain (including positive radius, signed EV/contrast, temperature and named parameter bounds); gain uses a nonnegative display range adapted to its rest level. Once keys exist, the original sampled-curve range and existing source rules resume. Deleting the last key or undoing first-key creation keeps the graph accessible, so source animation can be recreated without switching controls.
