The panel calls the authenticated ready-import API with captured source revisions, font bindings and the logical-ID option; failed verification never falls back to ordinary import.

Refresh, file/selection/mode changes invalidate review. Account changes clear private choices and cancel pending requests. Catalogue loading and conversion reject a response if the editor document/project/revision, caller context or import inputs changed. Revision changes are now part of the import identity even when document bytes are unchanged. The existing adoption path opens the verified report as a new unsaved project with one Undo/Redo step. The previous blanket prepared-mask warning has been replaced by guidance for selecting saved image masks.

Validation: 24 targeted frontend tests pass across the mounted panel (15), source/destination identity selection (3), fonts (2), ordinary import API (2) and prepared import API (2). The mounted panel consumes an actual private RVM/SAM ready-import report and the actual authenticated project-list response captured from the backend qualification, selects the intended project among multiple masks sharing one physical file, adopts the logical-collision result and restores it with Undo/Redo. The backend capture test passes with real pinned models enabled. The optional capture is generated in `/tmp` (about 14 KiB), not committed as a fixture. Reproduction uses `CONCAT_READY_IMPORT_UI_CAPTURE_OUTPUT` for the backend test and `CONCAT_READY_IMPORT_UI_CAPTURE_INPUT` for the frontend test; that gate was explicitly enabled here.

Negative mounted cases cover failed verification, stale catalogue/convert results, account change with cancellation, changed source file choice and failed refresh. Legacy API assertions were updated to the already-existing explicit `preserveMediaIds: false` wire default. Scoped ESLint is clean, frontend typecheck reports zero errors/warnings and `git diff --check` passes. The panel was rerun against the final real project-list capture (all 15 cases pass).

This is a mounted component plus captured HTTP-data bridge, not a live browser-to-server visual/quality acceptance run. Prepared video stores/bindings, derived-asset FillSlot reanalysis and wider RemoveMedia/rebinding history/lifecycle combinations remain open, together with broader codec/HDR/segmentation quality, template packs and full WeftCut/Filmcraft/Concat parity.

### Verified video-store transfer between saved slots — core implementation, partial (2026-11-03)

The internal video registry can now grant a different saved logical slot independent authority over an existing verified store. Both contexts must be editable at the expected revisions and reference the same registered physical source. Source restore verifies the encoded source, manifest, complete immutable parent chain and masks. Transfer pins the exact restored publication receipt rather than looking up a potentially newer, unverified generation after restoration. Unpublished cache changes cannot supply that receipt; empty stores cannot establish a transferred model choice.

An immediate SQLite transaction rechecks both projects' roles, revisions and physical source references, requires the exact verified source registration, then inserts/reuses a target registry row and updates the target model choice together. Concurrent/repeated transfers converge on one target row. Published files are shared unchanged, with no mask-byte copying or generation-directory creation/removal. The original project's model choice and document remain separate. Transfer still requires source authority on retries; a target that already owns a transferred store can restore it independently after origin-project access is revoked or origin rows are deleted.

The registry qualification runs legacy and logical-ID variants over a 65-generation parent chain. It covers target model-choice SQL failure/rollback, concurrent and repeated transfer, stale source/target revisions, outsider and target-viewer refusal, cancellation, changed source bytes, corrupted masks and a different registered file with identical bytes. Directory counts remain unchanged for transfer. Removing origin rows through a database cascade leaves target restoration and cache identity intact. This is not a filesystem garbage-collection qualification.

The real pinned Selfie HTTP case transfers its saved source store to a new project's differently named logical slot with every inference engine disabled. Before transfer that project's mask provider refuses; afterward provider identity and actual native preview pixels match the original verified result. Existing source preview, activation and FFV1 export gates continue to pass in that case.

This is registry ownership transfer between already saved projects. It is not yet prepared-video Concat import, and no new public import/UI action is exposed here. Unsaved import provenance, target clip/settings/range qualification, temporal-region resource reservations/rebinding, atomic orchestration with the final project save, and wider lifecycle/garbage collection work remain necessary. The full feature-transfer goal remains incomplete.

Validation: four backend tests pass with the real-model gate explicitly enabled: legacy 65-generation transfer, logical 65-generation transfer, empty-store refusal and the actual Selfie HTTP/preview/export case. Final registry cases also verify target-viewer refusal, rejection of retry after source-role revocation, and target cache invalidation after source-byte mutation. The final complete four-case run passes after the empty-store guard. `git diff --check` is clean. No frontend/public prepared-video completion is claimed by this core milestone.

### Atomic temporal-region ownership transfer — core implementation, partial (2026-11-03)

Verified video-store transfer can now retain temporal smart regions in the same immediate transaction as the target cache registration and family choice. It verifies each source snapshot against the original logical source/video hash, decodes and hashes its authorized movie, deduplicates repeated snapshot verification, enforces the existing 64-GiB staging/1024-region limits and rebases original/mask logical IDs without changing timestamps, prompts or mask identities. Existing target source bindings cannot be overwritten by a differently owned region file. Source region authority is rechecked inside the transaction; failed reservation rolls back the cache and family choice as well.

An additive `concat_video_project_region_refs` table records target project, original logical source/video hash, logical mask ID, physical library ID and encoded mask hash. The older unique ownership constraint in `person_video_project_resources` remains unchanged. Shared references persist across reopening and cascade only with their own target project. This avoids transferring ownership away from the source project or duplicating a registered mask movie.

Temporal-region restoration now resolves live logical mask bindings and exact snapshot-specific shared reservations. A reservation identifies immutable historical bytes even if a live bin alias is later rebound; full preview/export also requires the requested document's explicit mask mapping to agree with that verified file. Historical restoration therefore survives a saved stroke Undo and inactive mask-slot rebinding, while a forged requested mapping refuses. Original-video slot removal/rebinding and every derived-asset history combination are not established by this gate.

The extended actual reverse-VFR SAM/RVM case transfers brush/eraser regions into a different logical source and mask alias with models disabled. It checks SQL rollback, wrong source/hash/file/target-binding refusal, repeated transfer with one reservation and unchanged library/generation counts, temporary-stage cleanup after failure/success, saved adoption/Undo, live alias rebinding and model-free native preview. Source-space RGBA (including hidden RGB) is compared separately from composed-frame RGBA. Composed source/target previews match for one visible brush and for brush plus eraser. A second transfer uses only the intermediate project's shared history, then still restores after that intermediate project's database row is deleted.

Large verification/SQL futures are explicitly owned on the heap; the growing test exposed debug worker-stack overflow, which is fixed without increasing stack limits. The final ordinary-stack qualification passes all nine backend cases: incremental registry/empty-store gates (3), additive shared-reference schema/reopen/isolation (1), actual SAM/RVM CFR/VFR/earlier-audio cases (4), and the actual Selfie logical video preview/export case (1). Every model-dependent ignore gate was enabled. `git diff --check` passes.

These are internal saved-project ownership and renderer gates. Public prepared-video Concat conversion, unsaved import provenance, target clip/settings/coverage qualification and atomic orchestration with final document save remain to implement. Cross-space cloning, complete cache/retired-asset garbage collection, broader codec/HDR/segmentation-quality acceptance and full cross-application parity also remain open.

### Prepared video cutout conversion — trusted domain core, partial (2026-11-03)

`import_with_ready_bindings` now accepts server-owned still and video preparations together. `ReadyVideoBinding` is deliberately non-deserializable and assumes its caller has verified store coverage and region ownership. The ordinary public import path still refuses unresolved cutouts; clients cannot submit trusted video bindings as an import-request field.

Video preparation requires the registered original descriptor, captured settings and subject to match the destination. The bound family/settings and temporal snapshots are validated before rewriting IDs. Video placements retain their original source slot; snapshot original IDs follow the logical slot, and temporal mask IDs receive independent deterministic aliases when they collide with source media or still assets. Explicit root library bindings retain the physical region file, and existing media records are not overwritten. Source/model/runtime hashes, prompts, VFR grids and region identities remain unchanged. Missing/unused/stale or mismatched video preparations produce no partial project and retain the original Concat document.

Native binding changes only the clip's video-cutout selection and adds its verified region descriptors. It preserves ordinary conversion of audio, fades, source timing, pose and existing track/clip fields. Image media-version pairs and video mask bindings coexist without sharing a clip version; duplicate still/video destinations refuse. The original still-only API remains a wrapper over the new domain core with no video preparations.

Validation: 33 backend cases pass: prepared video admission (5), existing prepared still admission (6), logical media (3), ordinary project import (18) and the actual Selfie logical video case (1). The video cases cover timeline-scoped alias slots, physical legacy IDs, VFR mask collisions, source/subject/settings/hash/descriptor failures, mixed image/video preparations and deep equality of non-cutout clip audio/timing/pose fields against ordinary conversion. The actual pinned Selfie case converts Concat video settings, saves the native result, observes provider refusal before cache ownership transfer, transfers the verified store and renders the imported scene with every model disabled; preview pixels match the verified source result.

The formerly optional mounted ordinary-import request gate was explicitly enabled using a fresh request emitted by the mounted panel test (one frontend case passes); its backend HTTP conversion also passes. The 659-byte request and 1741-byte project output remain temporary files, not checked-in fixtures. `git diff --check` passes.

This completes the schema/conversion core, not public prepared-video import. Saved video-reference verification, unsaved preview/export provenance, final-save/cache/region atomic orchestration and UI selection still need implementation. The VFR region converter is qualified by schema/identity cases here; real SAM store/region transfer and rendering were qualified separately in the preceding milestone. Full codec/clock/HDR/quality coverage, templates and complete cross-application parity remain open.

### Saved video cache origin references (partial import bridge)

Native per-clip video bindings can retain an optional saved owner reference
(project, expected revision, logical source, and logical region aliases).
Preview and export resolve the owner's registered stores after checking editor
access, revision, physical source bindings, source/model/runtime identities and
verified temporal region files. A reference grants no access. Cache and region
provider keys include their owning namespace; preview rechecks all owner projects
after rendering, and export repeats provider validation before publication.
Trusted prepared-video conversion rekeys target region aliases while preserving
the saved owner's namespace. No inference or ownership transfer occurs on read.

Qualification includes real Selfie draft preview and export without savedProject,
SAM brush/eraser draft preview with renamed temporal regions, stale owner and
unauthorized actor refusals, and frontend round-trip/schema checks. The public
prepared-video import producer/selector and atomic final-save ownership adoption
remain open; this bridge does not establish complete Concat parity.

### Public prepared-video import references (partial workflow)

`POST /api/compositions/concat-project/import-ready` also accepts
`preparedVideos`, using the same source-project/composition/clip/revision
reference shape as `preparedStills`. Either or both lists may be supplied.
The server reads the selected saved clip, requires matching destination cutout
settings, restores the registered model store, verifies each temporal snapshot
and physical file access, and constructs the portable owner reference itself.
The source is reverified after conversion. Client paths and mask assertions are
not accepted. Reading and conversion create no new assets or saved projects.
Referenced drafts must first acquire their own saved cache ownership before
being selected as another import source; transitive origin grants are absent.

The frontend API supports mixed still/video references. Qualification covers a
real Selfie HTTP import, immediate model-free preview, equality with trusted
conversion after removing only the owner reference, stale/missing/duplicate
selection refusals, and preservation of the library inventory. The visible
video selector, atomic final-save adoption, and public-route temporal-region
qualification remain open.

### Prepared-video selection in the import panel

The visible Concat importer now requires a saved video-mask selection for every
video cutout destination, alongside existing still selections. Choices resolve
saved logical sources to their physical library files, preserve composition/clip
scope, and exclude imported origin references that have not acquired their own
cache ownership. Conversion sends mixed references to the authenticated route;
server validation remains authoritative. Catalogue changes, file binding changes,
editor revisions, and account changes invalidate review state. Changing accounts
clears both private catalogues and aborts outstanding requests.

Qualification: the real Selfie backend test writes an optional temporary capture
of its authenticated project list and import response. A mounted panel test
consumes that capture, selects the source clip, sends its references, and adopts
the returned native project with one Undo/Redo step. The generated JSON remains
outside the repository. Video failure/account-change tests and existing still,
media-binding, and API tests pass. Atomic final-save ownership adoption and
public-route temporal-region qualification remain open.

### Transaction boundary for final-save adoption (infrastructure)

Verified video transfer now has an opaque preparation stage independent of an
already-saved target project. It verifies the source store and temporal region
files against the proposed target document. Registration accepts the caller's
SQLite connection, so a future save can insert/update its document, source
inventory and memberships, then register every prepared store in that same
transaction. Registration does not commit. It rechecks both project authorities,
source registrations and region reservations, and requires the committed target
document to match the verified plan's document identity. Existing standalone
transfer uses these same stages inside its own immediate transaction.

This is the transaction boundary needed by final-save adoption, not a claim that
the create/update project ports already invoke adoption. Those ports and removal
of imported origin references on successful save remain open.

### Atomic adoption during project save

The runtime composition-project create/update ports now prepare imported video
origins before writing. They remove origin references from the final document
and register the verified stores, family choices and temporal-region reservations
inside the same SQLite transaction as the document, source inventory and project
memberships. Any registration error rolls back the save. The prepared plan is
bound to the exact final document and source hash; registration rechecks saved
source authority. Updating a project from its own previous-revision origin is
supported without retaining a stale self-reference. The frontend already applies
the canonical document returned by save.

Real Selfie qualification covers create/update rollback under a controlled SQL
choice failure, successful canonical saves, stale update rejection, owned-cache
preview and same-project origin adoption. Real SAM qualification covers rollback
under a region-reservation failure and successful shared temporal-region adoption;
after source-project editor access is revoked, the imported draft refuses that
source while the saved owner still renders identical pixels without inference.
Preparation and registration futures are boxed; the actual SAM case passes on
the normal debug worker stack after fixing a stack overflow found by this test.

These results qualify the HTTP create/update path. Archive/direct-DB adoption,
full imported-history lifecycle/GC, and reuse of already-adopted caches by older
Undo snapshots containing stale external origins remain outside this gate.

### Historical origin snapshots after adoption

When a saved project renders an older Undo snapshot containing an external
origin, the provider first checks that project's own exact source/model/runtime
registration and physical source binding. Every temporal region must also have
current or historical authority in that project. If so, the provider uses the
owned namespace and verifies its files normally. A missing registration may use
the explicit external origin; corrupted owned data is an error, with no fallback.
A stale saved revision or revoked target editor role is rejected.

The update save path uses the same ownership decision. An old origin snapshot
can therefore be saved again from the adopted namespace after external source
access is revoked; the returned document remains free of external origins.
Real Selfie and SAM cases exercise historical preview and update after revocation,
and Selfie checks that a forged owned manifest registration refuses even when
the external source remains valid. Provider loading and ownership selection use
boxed futures; the SAM scenario passes on the normal debug stack. Archive/direct
DB adoption and the wider imported-history lifecycle/GC remain unqualified.

### Portable video-store transport (archive infrastructure)

A standalone streaming video-store transport now flattens verified incremental
cache generations into one path-free manifest and sequential mask planes. Its
identity includes encoded source, model, runtime and the complete cache identity.
The reader requires an expected identity, checks lengths/frame budgets and exact
EOF, stages privately, and restores every run through the existing verifier.
Imported staging is removed on error/drop; explicit publication can retain a
verified standalone generation after staging is dropped. The codec itself grants
no project access or registrations.

Qualification includes a 65-generation round trip and durable republication,
independent nonblank mask planes compared byte-for-byte, deterministic re-export,
source mutation on export, empty-store refusal, truncated/trailing/corrupt data,
wrong source/cache identities, cancellation and byte-budget refusals. Tests use
small generated files; no large fixtures are checked in.

The `.veproj` HTTP archive currently still transports document and media records
only. Attaching these cache payloads to the archive manifest, preserving aggregate
archive limits, and registering imported stores atomically remain open. This
transport is an implementation prerequisite, not completed archive parity.

### Version-two archive cache records (format layer)

The `.veproj` reader/writer now supports version two with separate video-cache
records after media records. Each manifest entry names a logical source and the
portable source/model/runtime/cache identity, byte length and SHA-256 digest.
The format requires matching archived source bytes and clip bindings, complete
video-binding coverage, unique keys/tuples, exact record order and EOF. Media and
cache payloads share the existing aggregate byte limit. Version-one archives
retain their original header and omit the optional cache field.

The archive inventory validator also now uses the native physical-source
inventory for nested projects instead of comparing logical source names to file
IDs. Native dependency validation checks the scoped logical references.

Qualification: six existing archive HTTP tests plus flat/logical version-two
round trips with a real portable-codec payload, restored nonblank probabilities,
version-one compatibility, corrupt/truncated/trailing records, duplicate/wrong
bindings, aggregate limits and staging cleanup. The HTTP import route explicitly
rejects cache-bearing archives until atomic publication/registration is wired;
it cannot silently discard their caches. Automatic HTTP export collection and
atomic HTTP restore remain open.

### Automatic HTTP archive export of video stores

The archive download route now collects all bound video stores, including those
on disabled/copy clips and in non-active compositions. It uses the shared saved
provider to verify ownership, source/model/runtime identity and temporal regions,
then writes one portable payload per distinct binding. Identical bindings share
one record; conflicting stores for one tuple refuse export. Cache bytes and media
share the archive limit. Projects without video bindings keep version one.

Only the archived document loses external origin references; the saved project
is unchanged. All provider authorities and the exported project's revision,
document and physical inventory are checked again before returning the file.
Private cache payloads and source snapshots are cleaned on failure or completion.
The collector uses existing analysis admission, cancellation and archive deadlines.

Qualification: 13 backend tests pass. Actual model-free Selfie HTTP export covers
logical slots, disabled copies, record deduplication, restored plane equality,
missing-store refusal and staging cleanup. Actual model-free SAM export succeeds
after source-project access is revoked and includes both the portable automatic
store and the hash-matching temporal-region media. Existing version-one HTTP and
version-two format tests remain green. Atomic HTTP import of these cache records
is still open and explicitly rejected until its registration path is ready.

### HTTP restore of self-contained video archives

Version-two HTTP imports now restore portable automatic stores and verify every
referenced temporal-region movie before granting project ownership. Physical
media IDs are replaced while logical slots and source-time snapshots are retained.
Encoded source hashes, portable identities, model/runtime layouts and region file/
plane hashes must match. External origin references are removed from the imported
document. No original projects, cache registrations or inference models are needed.

New standalone generations are guarded until project creation succeeds. Media
placement in the target Space completes before the database commit; the project,
source inventory, automatic-store rows, model choices and historical region refs
are registered together. A failure removes the newly published cache generations,
library records, source files and staging. Target Space write access is checked
before work and again within the creation transaction. Import continues in its
owned publication task if the HTTP client disconnects.

Qualification: 18 integration tests pass, including actual Selfie imports with
both logical and physical IDs into a fresh storage instance, and actual SAM/VFR
region import into another fresh instance. All inference engines are disabled at
the destination; preview pixels and cache identities match the source. The tests
also cover valid outer archive checksums around corrupt inner mask bytes, forced
cache/region registration failures, a target-role demotion inside the transaction,
viewer refusal, and absence of residual project rows, cache rows, library metadata,
source files, cache generations or staging after failures. Version-one HTTP and
version-two framing tests remain green. This qualifies these archive round trips;
whole-project feature parity and the wider history/GC/platform gates remain open.

Additional focused unit gates for this restore change: all 11 archive tests and
all 8 composition-project DB tests pass. The archive unsupported-version test now
uses version three because version two is supported.

### Historical temporal files survive bin changes

Library deletion now counts exact temporal-region reservations as saved-project
ownership, alongside current source references. Both shared imported reservations
and legacy `sam-video-regions` reservations retain their files while their project
exists. Multiple snapshots/current references count once per owning project;
orphan legacy rows do not retain files after project deletion. An additive index
supports physical-region ownership lookup.

Qualification: all nine composition-project DB unit tests and eleven integration
tests pass. The cold SAM archive case rebinds the inactive live mask slot to the
original video, removing the mask file from the saved physical source inventory.
Library deletion still returns conflict, and the historical requested snapshot
renders identical pixels through its imported reservation. After deleting the
last owning project, the count is zero and library deletion succeeds. A separate
DB case covers two owners, repeated snapshots and a stale legacy reservation.
This fixes temporal-region retention; complete original-media history ownership
and global cache/asset garbage collection remain separate unfinished gates.

### Physical originals retained by published video stores

A new project/source/hash/physical-file reservation records the actual registered
original when automatic stores are published, progressively appended, transferred,
or imported from an archive. Reservation and cache registration share the same
transaction; a failed reservation cannot advance the publication cursor or leave
a registered cache pointing at a removed generation. Library reference counts
include these reservations, deduplicated by project, with cascading release when
the last owner project is deleted. An additive physical-owner lookup index is
included.

Qualification: ten composition-project DB tests and seventeen integration tests
pass. Generated registry tests reject original-reservation insertion and verify
cache/generation rollback, safe retry and one original reservation across 65
incremental generations. Cold Selfie archive tests for logical and physical IDs
replace the current document with an empty composition: original deletion stays
blocked until the owner project is deleted, then succeeds. Failed archive imports
also leave no original-reservation rows. Existing SAM, archive and migration gates
remain green.

This gate retains original bytes; rendering a historical logical slot after its
current binding is removed/rebound still needs reservation-aware resolution.
Legacy registrations without a verified physical reservation are not guessed or
backfilled from ambiguous old bindings. Those recovery and full GC gates remain
unfinished.

### Historical original resolution for preview and resave

Saved video providers can now resolve the physical original named by a requested
historical snapshot after its live logical slot is removed or rebound. Access
requires current project editor membership and revision, plus either the matching
live binding or an exact project/logical-source/video-hash/physical-file reservation.
The original bytes are fingerprinted before and after restoring the exact model/
runtime store. Temporal providers use the same original authority while retaining
their separate snapshot-specific region reservations.

Owned-origin selection and transfer preparation share this resolution, so saving
an older imported snapshot can reuse the adopted namespace without contacting an
obsolete external origin. Registration still checks both endpoint authorities;
the target must have the restored physical source in its transaction's inventory.

Qualification: all sixteen affected integration tests pass. Cold Selfie imports
with both logical and physical IDs, and a cold SAM/VFR import, replace their current
document with an empty composition. Their historical snapshots still render the
same pixels and can be saved again with a stale external origin removed. Stale
revisions, changed source hashes, viewer roles and a different unregistered file
containing identical bytes refuse access. Existing cache-transfer, archive and
version-one compatibility cases stay green. Legacy inactive slots without a proven
physical reservation and the remaining history/GC/platform gates remain open.

### Verified adoption of legacy current bindings

Restoring an older registered store now materializes its missing physical-original
reservation only after verifying the current logical binding, encoded source hash,
complete cache generation and final source authority. The guarded SQL statement
requires the same project revision/editor, current physical source inventory and
exact source/model/runtime/generation/manifest registration. Existing reservations
skip writes. Equivalent duplicate legacy registrations select one proof and do
not create duplicate ownership. No generation is republished.

All sixteen affected integration tests pass. Real cold Selfie (logical and physical
IDs) and SAM/VFR cases remove their original reservation to simulate legacy data,
add a duplicate receipt registration, and verify that wrong source hashes and a
controlled SQL failure leave no reservation. Successful preview creates exactly
one reservation, after which source removal, historical preview and resave work.
Archive, cache-transfer and compatibility gates remain green. Missing historical
bindings without a current verified physical mapping still refuse; this migration
does not infer provenance from matching bytes elsewhere in the library.

### Fill all open-template slots in one history operation

The project-media panel now offers “Заполнить все слоты шаблона” once replacements
are chosen for every placeholder. The state operation snapshots the requested
mapping, rejects missing or extra slots before probing, and runs the existing
ACL-bound native FillSlot endpoint sequentially against a private staged document.
No intermediate document or render-cache invalidation reaches the editor. A later
slot failure preserves the entire live document, rendered outputs and history;
success commits one Undo/Redo entry for all fills. Account/library context changes
and project close invalidate the staged operation. Each replacement still uses the
existing server probe and source-access checks; there is no new media publication
or project save.

Twelve frontend tests pass across the mounted project-media controls and slot API:

These component tests mock HTTP; they do not establish a fresh real-server batch
or browser qualification. Template bundle packaging/gallery/posters, derived-asset
FillSlot rebinding and full source-application parity remain open.

Final checks: Svelte typecheck reports zero errors/warnings; production build
passes (39.54s, existing chunk warnings); design-token and listener-lifecycle
checks and `git diff --check` pass. Backend media semantics are unchanged.

### Native template slot inventory and active-timeline presentation

The read-only `/compositions/nested-template-info` endpoint validates a supplied
native project and returns its selected timeline canvas and placeholder inventory.
Rust orders slots by first authored placement on that timeline and sums their
editorial durations, including repeated, hidden/muted and retimed clips. A slot
unused on that timeline is retained with zero seconds. It does not count another
timeline or recursively count child placements. Equal first-use times follow the
canonical native media registry order; preserving an imported Concat bin's original
array order for ties is not implemented by the BTreeMap registry.

The project-media panel requests this inventory only when expanded, displays media
kind and summed seconds, and uses the returned slot ordering. Changing project,
active timeline, collapsing or unmounting cancels observation of the old request.
The frontend validates the complete placeholder identity/kind set and nonnegative
finite durations. This endpoint takes an in-memory document and performs no file
lookup, copying or library publication; it confers no source access.

Sixteen frontend tests pass across project-media controls and metadata/slot APIs,
including mounted active-timeline display, ordering and stale-response refusal.
Scoped lint passes. Bundle packing, font/media copying, gallery/posters, standalone
instantiation and derived-asset FillSlot rebinding remain open. This milestone does
not establish a complete template-bundle workflow or whole-application parity.

Final validation: six backend tests pass, including the actual HTTP route,
retimed authored-duration accounting, hidden/muted placements, inactive/unused
media, default root, unknown timeline, invalid project and project-media
regressions. The initial test used pre-import timeline names; it was corrected to
the converter's canonical timeline IDs without changing production admission.
Frontend typecheck reports zero errors/warnings; production build passes in 18.25s
with existing chunk warnings. Design-token, listener-lifecycle and diff checks pass.

### Native template bundle codec (qualified core; workflow incomplete)

`template_bundle` introduces a stored ZIP containing a native `template.json` and
an exact allowlist of design asset records. Packing validates the project, makes
canonical media records for legacy timeline sources, deduplicates physical design
files and replaces their library bindings with package-local keys. Placeholder
bindings are removed and their original bytes are not requested or copied. A
physical file deliberately used by a separate non-placeholder design item still
ships for that design item. Native compositions, embedded font data and LUTs stay
in the native document rather than passing through the narrower Concat exporter.

Packing requires the caller to supply exactly the authorized design input set,
fingerprints each file and verifies it again while streaming. Input paths belong
to the caller and are never accepted from an imported manifest. Reading validates
schema, project, inventory and SHA-256/length bounds, stages only named records
under generated filenames, and owns staged files through RAII cleanup. Manifest
and total asset budgets reuse project archive limits. Slot rebindings, media
probing, durable gallery storage and project creation are not implemented by this
codec. Video-mask stores explicitly refuse until their cache payloads can be
packaged; an apparently complete template must not lose those masks.


Final core gate: ten backend tests pass (four package tests, three template-info
and three project-media regressions). Real generated PNG bytes round-trip exactly;
two logical design aliases share one payload; slot bindings and physical source
identities are absent from the manifest; all native timeline surfaces remain
unchanged. Cases cover empty templates, missing/wrong input inventories, changed
source bytes during streaming, valid-ZIP/corrupt-payload digest refusal, extra
path-like records, missing assets, retained slot bindings, unsupported schema,
truncation and staged cleanup after failure/drop. The first malformed-manifest
test helper read a key after removing its inventory; its construction order was
fixed and the full gate rerun. No runtime admission was weakened. Diff checks pass.
This is a native codec gate, not yet an HTTP export/import or gallery acceptance.

### Saved native template HTTP download

`GET /composition-projects/:id/template` now streams a `.vktemplate` from a saved
native project. Bearer and session-cookie authorization follow project archive
navigation. The exporter plans the exact design inventory, checks every resource
against the saved project's physical index and its current source access, then
runs the codec in a blocking worker. That worker owns both output cleanup and its
admission permit even if the HTTP request disappears. Before responding, the
handler rechecks resource entries/paths/revisions, access, current session and
saved project revision/document/source index. No placeholder file is opened.
Dropping or consuming the response deletes its temporary archive.

The native workspace includes a dedicated “Скачать шаблон сохранённой версии”
control; it navigates directly to the encoded download URL without fetching a
multi-gigabyte Blob. Its status explicitly identifies the saved version rather
than implying that unsaved changes have been packed.

Eight backend tests pass: actual HTTP export plus package and template-info
regressions. A generated PNG is exactly preserved; a missing original slot file
does not block export. Anonymous/outsider access and missing design files refuse;
cookie download and both response consumption/drop clean staging; saved document
is unchanged. Sixteen frontend tests pass across the isolated mounted download
control, template API and project-media controls; scoped lint passes. An attempted
full native-workspace mount with generic API fixtures hit an effect-update-depth
error and is not a passing whole-workspace qualification. The dedicated control
is tested without substituting those renderer/playback fixtures. Import,
instantiation, gallery/posters, video-mask packaging and live browser acceptance
remain open.

Final scoped checks: Svelte typecheck reports zero errors/warnings; production
build passes (22.95s, existing chunk warnings). Design-token, listener-lifecycle
and diff checks pass. The full native-workspace mount issue above remains an
unresolved verification gap rather than a passing browser claim.

### Full native-workspace template download mount

The earlier effect-depth failure was traced to the workspace test harness using
Svelte's server `untrack` while mounting browser components from the client entry.
Its playback-control regression tests already replace that one export with the
client implementation. The workspace harness now does the same; production
reactivity and playback code are unchanged.

A complete mounted native workspace now draws an exact generated RGBA response,
downloads the encoded saved-template URL, displays the status and preserves its
document. Catalog requests deliberately return HTTP 503 to exercise unavailable
optional services rather than returning invalid `[]` page shapes. Native duration
and preview APIs have typed mock responses; clicking download does not restart
their effects. Real template HTTP/binary behavior remains covered by the preceding
backend export test, not by these mocks. All 29 tests across the complete workspace
suite, playback, preview, template control and template API pass without unhandled
errors. The historical mount failure is resolved for this harness; this is still
not a live browser-to-server qualification or completion of template import,
gallery, posters or video-mask packaging.

The final strengthened full-workspace suite passes all twelve tests after adding
an exact drawn-pixel assertion. Svelte typecheck and scoped lint pass; diff checks
pass. No production files changed in this qualification milestone.

### Atomic native template instantiation core

A pure `template_bundle::instantiate` operation assembles a project from a
validated package manifest, newly allocated design-file bindings and server-probed
slot replacements. It requires the exact design key set, distinct fresh physical
identities for distinct design records, and exactly one replacement for every
placeholder. All rebinding and canonical native FillSlot operations run on a
private document; a later failure returns no partial project. Logical design/slot
IDs remain editorial IDs while physical library ownership changes. The final
project has no placeholders and passes native dependency and saved-project
physical inventory validation.

This operation does not probe files, grant access, publish library entries or
commit a project; its future HTTP caller must verify the package and media, own
those resources and perform publication/rollback. It preserves the existing
FillSlot admission boundaries, including derived-media and video-mask refusals.
HTTP upload, durable template gallery and standalone project publication remain
unfinished.

Final qualification passes seventeen backend tests with ignored runtime tests
explicitly enabled: six package/instantiation tests, ten native FillSlot tests
and one actual template HTTP export test. A real packaged PNG is parsed before
assembly; two filled slots retain logical IDs and editorial windows in both
active and shelved timelines, including image-to-video conversion. Incomplete
mapping, unfilled slots, reuse of package keys as physical bindings and a later
incompatible replacement return no project and leave the template unchanged.
Existing actual FFmpeg moving-video/audio tests still verify new physical files,
held last frames and silence after EOF. The initial replacement fixture omitted
its inert `library:` path; it was fixed without changing runtime admission and
the full gate was rerun. Diff checks pass. Durable project creation remains the
next integration boundary, not a completion claim for template instantiation UI.
